36996-mystic-immanence-the-indwelling-sp.creator: Unknown
36996-mystic-immanence-the-indwelling-sp.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. e material universe is the visible thought of God. What is the principle by which everything came into being? Physical science has now reduced all material things to a primary ether, universally distributed, whose innumerable particles are in absolute equilibrium.[#]  The initial movement, then, which began to concentrate material substances out of the ether could not have originated with the particles themselves, and we are logically compelled to acknowledge the presence of a Creative Intelligence exercising volition.

arxiv-2109-04227.title: Evaluation of imputation techniques with varying percentage of missing data
arxiv-2109-04227.creator: Seema Sangari, Herman E. Ray
arxiv-2109-04227.description: Abstract Missing data is a common problem which has consistently plagued statisticians and applied analytical researchers. While replacement methods like mean-based or hot deck imputation have been well researched, emerging imputation techniques enabled through improved computational resources have had limited formal assessment.

arxiv-2202-02706.title: A Note on Holevo quantity of S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) -invariant states
arxiv-2202-02706.creator: Yao-Kun Wang, Li-Zhu Ge, Shao-Ming Fei, Zhi-Xi Wang
arxiv-2202-02706.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yao-Kun Wang, Li-Zhu Ge, Shao-Ming Fei, Zhi-Xi Wang. The Holevo quantity and the S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) -invariant states have particular importance in quantum information processing. We calculate analytically the Holevo quantity for bipartite systems composed of spin- j j and spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} subsystems with S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) symmetry, when the projective measurements are performed on the spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} subsystem.

arxiv-2203-02211.title: Gamma-Shadowed Two-Ray with Diffuse Power Composite Fading Model
arxiv-2203-02211.creator: Pamela Njemcevic and Almir Maric
arxiv-2203-02211.description: Abstract In this paper, a novel gamma-shadowed two-ray with diffuse power (GS-TWDP) composite fading model is proposed. The model is intended for modeling propagation in the emerging wireless networks working at millimeter wave (mmWave) frequencies, and is obtained as a combination of TWDP distribution for description of multipath effects and gamma distribution for modeling variations due to shadowing.

arxiv-2209-04259.title: Knowledge-based Deep Learning for Modeling Chaotic Systems
arxiv-2209-04259.creator: Zakaria Elabid, Tanujit Chakraborty, Abdenour Hadid
arxiv-2209-04259.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zakaria Elabid, Tanujit Chakraborty, Abdenour Hadid. Deep Learning has received increased attention due to its unbeatable success in many fields, such as computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and most recently in simulating multiphysics problems and predicting nonlinear dynamical systems. However, modeling and forecasting the dynamics of chaotic systems remains an open research problem since training deep learning models requires big data, which is not always available in many cases.

arxiv-2212-04589.title: Optimizing Integrated Information with a Prior Guided Random Search Algorithm
arxiv-2212-04589.creator: Eduardo C. Garrido-Merchán 1, Javier Sánchez-Cañizares 2
arxiv-2212-04589.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Eduardo C. Garrido-Merchán 1, Javier Sánchez-Cañizares 2. Integrated information theory (IIT) is a theoretical framework that provides a quantitative measure to estimate when a physical system is conscious, its degree of consciousness, and the complexity of the qualia space that the system is experiencing. Formally, IIT rests on the assumption that if a surrogate physical system can fully embed the phenomenological properties of consciousness, then the system properties must be constrained by the properties of the qualia being experienced.

arxiv-2308-16230.title: Qudit Machine Learning
arxiv-2308-16230.creator: Sebastián Roca-Jerat, Juan Román-Roche, David Zueco
arxiv-2308-16230.description: Abstract We present a comprehensive investigation into the learning capabilities of a simple d d -level system (qudit). Our study is specialized for classification tasks using real-world databases, specifically the Iris, breast cancer, and MNIST datasets. We explore various learning models in the metric learning framework, along with different encoding strategies.

arxiv-2401-10177.title: New-generation Maximum Entropy Method (ngMEM): a Lagrangian-based algorithm for dynamic reconstruction of interferometric data New-generation Maximum Entropy Method (ngMEM): a Lagrangian-based algorithm for dynamic reconstruction of interferometric data –
arxiv-2401-10177.creator: Alejandro Mus, Ivan Martí-Vidal
arxiv-2401-10177.description: Abstract Imaging interferometric data in radio astronomy requires the use of non-linear algorithms that rely on different assumptions on the source structure and may produce non-unique results. This is especially true for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations, where the sampling of Fourier space is very sparse.

arxiv-2404-02360.title: FraGNNet: A Deep Probabilistic Model for Tandem Mass Spectrum Prediction
arxiv-2404-02360.creator: Adamo Young ayoung@cs.toronto.edu, Fei Wang fw4@ualberta.ca, David S Wishart dwishart@ualberta.ca, Bo Wang bowang@vectorinstitute.ai, Russell Greiner rgreiner@ualberta.ca, Hannes Röst hannes.rost@utoronto.ca
arxiv-2404-02360.description: Abstract Compound identification from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data is a critical step in the analysis of complex mixtures. Typical solutions for the MS/MS spectrum to compound (MS2C) problem involve comparing the unknown spectrum against a library of known spectrum-molecule pairs, an approach that is limited by incomplete library coverage.

arxiv-2507-21224.title: Resummation of Cosmological Correlators and their UV-Regularization Preprint: LMU-ASC 18/25
arxiv-2507-21224.creator: Matthias Nowinski, and Ivo Sachs
arxiv-2507-21224.description: Abstract Cosmological correlators are important observables in cosmology. They are often approximated by de Sitter space correlators. In this paper, we give a first precise diagrammatical computation of higher loop diagrams to all orders for a conformally coupled scalar in four dimensions.

arxiv-2601-02518.title: Diffusion Computation versus Quantum Computation: A Comparative Model for Order Finding and Factoring
arxiv-2601-02518.creator: Carlos A. Cadavid
arxiv-2601-02518.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Carlos A. Cadavid. We study a hybrid computational model for integer factorization in which standard digital arithmetic is augmented by access to an iterated diffusion process on a finite graph. A diffusion step consists of applying a fixed local-averaging operator (a half-lazy random-walk matrix) to an ℓ 1 \ell^{1} -normalized state vector, together with a prescribed readout of a small number of coordinates.

pmc-10671467.title: Interaction of TSG101 with the PTAP Motif in Distinct Locations of Gag Determines the Incorporation of HTLV-1 Env into the Retroviral Virion
pmc-10671467.creator: Yosuke Maeda, Kazuaki Monde, Hiromi Terasawa, Yuetsu Tanaka, Tomohiro Sawa, József Tőzsér
pmc-10671467.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Human T-cell tropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) is known to be mainly transmitted by cell-to-cell contact due to the lower infectivity of the cell-free virion. However, the reasons why cell-free HTLV-1 infection is poor remain unknown. In this study, we found that the retrovirus pseudotyped with HTLV-1 viral envelope glycoprotein (Env) was infectious when human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) was used to produce the virus.

pmc-11269517.title: On Refining the SZZ Algorithm with Bug Discussion Data
pmc-11269517.creator: Pooja Rani, Fernando Petrulio, Alberto Bacchelli
pmc-11269517.description: ContextResearchers testing hypotheses related to factors leading to low-quality software often rely on historical data, specifically on details regarding when defects were introduced into a codebase of interest. The prevailing techniques to determine the introduction of defects revolve around variants of the SZZ algorithm.

pmc-12953727.title: COTPA Section 4 Compliance in Udupi City Municipal Corporation: An Exploratory Survey From Coastal Karnataka
pmc-12953727.creator: Nishu Singla, Vinissa Eliane Tauro, Krishanu Dutta, Ayan Pradhan, Ritesh Singla, Jishnu Pradeep, Bidisha Sarmah, Deepak Kumar Singhal, Ridhima Birmani Gaunkar
pmc-12953727.description: BackgroundThe Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003, prohibits smoking in public places under Section 4 to protect individuals from second‐hand smoke (SHS). However, compliance with this provision remains inconsistent across India.AimTo assess compliance with Section 4 of COTPA in public places in the Udupi City Municipal Corporation (UCMC) of Karnataka.

pmc-13031413.title: Enforcing a high success percentage interferes with reward-based motor learning
pmc-13031413.creator: Katinka van der Kooij, Nina M van Mastrigt, Moira van Leeuwen, Maaike R van der Horst, Joyce E Burger, Jeroen B J Smeets
pmc-13031413.description: Humans can adapt their movements based on binary reward feedback about success and failure. To engage in such ‘reward-based’ motor learning, the learner must encounter at least some failures, but it is unclear what percentage of failures is optimal. For learning, we hypothesize that a success percentage of 50% is optimal, as it provides the most information.

pmc-13193924.title: Extreme low temperature is the key meteorological limiting factor for winter wheat yield in Shihezi
pmc-13193924.creator: Shuai Zhang, Haonan Hu, Jingting Peng, Jianrong Zhai, Mingfeng Yang
pmc-13193924.description: IntroductionIn the background of global climate change, extreme weather events occur frequently, leading to various agricultural meteorological disasters worldwide. However, the key meteorological limiting factor for winter wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) production in Shihezi (Xingjiang, China) remains unclear. Clarifying this factor is a core prerequisite for ensuring regional food security.

pmc-13467223.title: Tracking Nano- and Microplastics in Plants: Uptake Pathways, Tissue Distribution, and Analytical Strategies from Microscopy to Spectroscopy
pmc-13467223.creator: Abdullah Maqsood, Ewa Łobos-Moysa, Amna Jameel, Ewa Dacewicz
pmc-13467223.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nano- and microplastics (NMPs) are now widely detected across agroecosystems and can act as physiological stressors in plants. Exposure occurs through contaminated soil, irrigation water, or airborne deposition, bringing particles into direct contact with roots and above-ground tissues. Reported entry routes include apoplastic transport, cracks formed at lateral root emergence, leaf stomata, and endocytosis once particles have crossed the cell wall.

pmc-13624170.title: Adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the Natural Disasters Picture System (NDPS) to the Spanish population
pmc-13624170.creator: Danae A. Mendoza, José M. Reales, Soledad Ballesteros
pmc-13624170.description: IntroductionClimate change is causing an increase in natural disasters and extreme weather events. This threat is impacting the mental health of those who experience it. However, empirical research in the Spanish context is limited by the lack of culturally adapted tools.
